question.problem:
A series RCL circuit has a source electromotive force (EMF) of $9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\,\text{V},$ a resistance of $18\,Ω,$ a capacitance of $0.002\,\text{F},$ and an inductance of $L=9\,\text{H}.$ Find the differential equation governing the amount of current $I$ (in amperes) in the circuit at time $t$ (in seconds).

*Hint: The voltage drop ${V}_{C}$ across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C},$ where $C$ is the capacitance measured in Farads.*
question.worked_solution:
The diagram for our circuit is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14186466/assets/a3bbe131778b11fe61a7e436d3d4729958bb207961ca9faaac91250cf4f2dde0.png)

The current $I,$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q,$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I=\frac{dq}{dt}
$$

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RCL circuit, there are three voltage drops:

- The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality $R=18\,Ω.$ So,

$$
{V}_{R}=18I.
$$

- The voltage drop across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C}.$ Therefore,

$$
{V}_{C}=\frac{q}{C}=\frac{q}{0.002}=500q.
$$

- The voltage drop across the inductor is proportional to the rate of change of current, with a constant of proportionality $L=9\,\text{H}.$ Hence,

$$
{V}_{L}=9\,\frac{dI}{dt}.
$$

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, these values are related by the equation

$$
9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)=18I+500q+9\,\frac{dI}{dt}.
$$

Differentiating with respect to $t,$ the differential equation governing the current in the circuit is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}(9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) & =\frac{d}{dt}(18I+500q+9\,\frac{dI}{dt}) \\ 27\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) & =18\,\frac{dI}{dt}+500\,\frac{dq}{dt}+9\,\frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

which, when substituting in $I=\frac{dq}{dt},$ gives

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}}+2\,\frac{dI}{dt}+\frac{500}{9}I=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).
$$
